events.title: Emperor Julian sets out to invade Persia
events.description: Julian left Antioch with a large army to attack the Sasanian Empire. He reached Ctesiphon but was killed during the retreat in June, and with him ended the last attempt to restore paganism.
events.html: Julian left Antioch with a large army to attack the Sasanian Empire. He reached Ctesiphon but was killed during the retreat in June, and with him ended the last attempt to restore paganism.

events.title: Nasir Khusraw sets out on his seven-year journey
events.description: The Persian poet and philosopher Nasir Khusraw set out on a pilgrimage to Mecca, taking an indirect route north toward the Caspian Sea. His account of the seven-year journey, the Safarnama, described the wealth of Fatimid Cairo.

events.title: Lithuania defeats the Livonian Order at Aizkraukle
events.description: Near Aizkraukle in present-day Latvia, the Grand Duchy of Lithuania under Traidenis defeated the Livonian branch of the Teutonic Order, killing 71 knights, including the grand master, Ernst von Rassburg. Duke Nameisis of the Semigallians then recognised Traidenis as suzerain.

events.title: Henry VII commissions John Cabot to seek new lands
events.description: Letters patent authorised the Venetian navigator to sail under the English flag in search of unknown lands. His 1497 voyage reached North America and later underpinned English claims there.

events.title: British soldiers kill five in the Boston Massacre
events.description: Soldiers fired into a crowd taunting them in King Street, killing five men, including Crispus Attucks. Paul Revere's engraving of the scene became powerful propaganda against British rule.
events.html: Soldiers fired into a crowd taunting them in King Street, killing five men, including Crispus Attucks. Paul Revere's engraving of the scene became powerful propaganda against British rule.

events.title: Churchill warns of an 'iron curtain' across Europe
events.description: Speaking at Fulton, Missouri, Winston Churchill declared that an iron curtain had descended across the continent from the Baltic to the Adriatic. The speech popularised the phrase and the Cold War divide.
events.html: Speaking at Fulton, Missouri, Winston Churchill declared that an iron curtain had descended across the continent from the Baltic to the Adriatic. The speech popularised the phrase and the Cold War divide.

events.title: Joseph Stalin dies
events.description: The Soviet dictator died four days after a stroke at his dacha near Moscow. His rule had brought rapid industrialisation and victory over Germany, but also famine, purges and millions of deaths.
events.html: The Soviet dictator died four days after a stroke at his dacha near Moscow. His rule had brought rapid industrialisation and victory over Germany, but also famine, purges and millions of deaths.

events.title: Alberto Korda photographs Che Guevara
events.description: At a Havana memorial for victims of a ship explosion, Korda captured Guevara's gaze in a photograph later titled 'Guerrillero Heroico'. It became one of the most reproduced images in the world.

events.title: Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty enters into force
events.description: The treaty committed nuclear powers not to spread weapons and others not to acquire them, while promoting peaceful nuclear energy. With 191 parties, it is the most widely joined arms control agreement.
